english_description: The scalar Poly1305 one-time authenticator with clamped-key initialization and streaming updates.

queries.english: Compute the Poly1305 tag for this one-time key and message.
Compute the Poly1305 tag while splitting the message at this offset.
queries.rust_sig: fn compute_tag_chunked(&self, key: &[u8; 32], message: &[u8], split_at: usize) -> Result<[u8; 16], CryptoError>

commands.english: Initialize the Poly1305 state with one 32-byte one-time key.
commands.rust_sig: fn set_key(&mut self, key: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<(), CryptoError>

commands.english: Add the next message bytes to the Poly1305 state.
commands.rust_sig: fn update(&mut self, input: &[u8]) -> Result<(), CryptoError>

commands.english: Finalize the Poly1305 state and return its tag.

constraints.english: Poly1305 initialization receives exactly one thirty-two-byte key.
Successful Poly1305 finalization returns exactly sixteen tag bytes.
Splitting the same message at a valid offset does not change its tag.
The chunk split offset is within the supplied message.
Authenticating a sequence of segments gives the tag of their concatenation.

adversary_table.scenario: Finalize messages of lengths 0, 1, 15, 16, and 17 bytes.
adversary_table.resolution: return a sixteen-byte tag for every successful finalization

adversary_table.scenario: Use a key with high and low bits that must be cleared by clamping.
adversary_table.resolution: apply the RFC clamp before processing message blocks

adversary_table.scenario: Split messages at offsets around a sixteen-byte boundary.
adversary_table.resolution: produce the same tag for one-shot and chunked processing

adversary_table.scenario: Set the split offset beyond the message length.
adversary_table.resolution: return an error without reading outside the message

adversary_table.scenario: Split the RFC test message into three segments at block and non-block offsets, including empty segments.
adversary_table.resolution: produce the same tag as one-shot authentication of the concatenated message

source_references.notes: Scalar initialization, block arithmetic, and finalization; SIMD providers are separate.
